The first, which deals with the powers of the Tupan of the Shanghai Municipal District, says that he must control the administrative affairs and supervise local self-government there. Included in his powers are the supervision of the district, control of the harbour, labour reforms, registration of the inhabitants and houses, control of fire brigades, anti-plague measures, public peace, foreign intercourse, certain monetary matters, public buildings and newly-constructed roads.

label: text
text: The Commissioner of Foreign Affairs at Shanghai and the Suprintendents of Police and Water Police and the Harbour Bureau are placed under the Tupan.

label: text
text: The second mandate deals with the system of local self-government in Shanghai and the powers of the local self-government institutions, which include supervision under the Tupan of roads, bridges, buildings, light trams, water works, telephones, sanitation, relief work, education, recreation, financial affairs, and the disposal and control of municipal property.

label: paragraph_title
text: General Strike Threat.

label: text
text:
The situation is tenser to-day, following a meeting attended by fifteen hundred, mostly students, at the Chinese Chamber of Commerce last evening, whereat many wild resolutions were passed.
A student named Ling Ku-yung presided. Members of the Chamber vainly attempted to keep down the excitement and moved that a special meeting, consisting of two delegates from each society represented, be appointed to deal with the business under discussion. The extremists demanded a motion in favour of a general strike also that the acting Chairman of the chamber, who was not present be called on to explain his attitude.
The extremists motion was carried a large unproviding action obviously being terrorised.

label: text
text: The meeting then sent a delegation to bring the acting Chairman who came subsequently, announcing under compulsion that the Chamber would to-day issue circular-stationing—"In view of the assassination of our brethren, we have decided on a general strike." The audience then shouted. "Let us overthrow modern Imperialism and abolish unequal treaties. Let Labourers, merchants and students join in one body and fight together in common cause."

label: text
text: Additional resolutions carried included: "Boycott of foreign banknotes; withdrawal of Chinese deposits from foreign banks; control of the Municipal police to be placed in Chinese hands; withdrawal of foreign war"

text: TO-DAY'S MEETING.

label: text
text:
An extraordinary general meeting of the Hongkong and Vhampa Dock Company, Limited, was held this morning for the purpose of confirming as special resolutions the resolutions in regard to the raising of new capital passed at a meeting held a few weeks ago.
Dr. F. H. Kew drew the attention of Mr. D. G. M. Bernard, the Chairman, to the wording of the resolution under which the directors were empowered to dispose of the unissued new shares as they thought fit. It was to be presumed, he said, that the shareholders were to go given the first opportunity of taking up the shares when it was decided to issue them.

label: text
text:
Causal at present prevail, but the situation depends upon the extent of the outside backing the rioters are receiving.
According to Chinese reports, $70,000 recently reached Shanghai for the purpose of subsidising the rioters.
The Council is prepared for almost any eventuality, and intends to hold a special meeting of rate-payers to tomorrow some of the resolutions of which the student proclamations rigorously oppose.
There were minor disturbances in the outlying districts this evening. Some arrests were made but there were uncasualties. Otherwise the city is further but considerable interest which is to the right of those arrested tomorrow.
Questions relating to the disposal of the unissued new shares in connection with the raising by the Doc Company of new capital were mentioned at a meeting to-day, the opinion being expressed that the shareholders were not sufficiently safeguarded by the phrasing of the resolution.

label: text
text: The Chairman: That would be a matter entirely for the directors. For instance, if we had fifty shares how could we offer them en bloc?

label: text
text: Dr. Kew: It is not a question of fifty but many more than fifty. I think they ought to be offered to shareholders and if they are not taken up the directors would do as they like with them. That seems to me the fair thing to do. I am referring to the unissued shares it is not proposed to deal with in the present issue.

label: text
text: The Chairman said he had only just realised Dr. Kew was referring to the unissued shares. He was afraid he could not bind his successors.

label: text
text: Dr. Kew: The shares may go up and I think the shareholders should have the chance before the general public. The shares might go up to premium and under the resolution the directors might take them all, for all the shareholders are to know.

Gunner Birbeck of Lyemum Battery who was alleged to have deserted on May 15, and to have given himself up at Kowloon City four days later, was charged with desertion and insubordination at a district court martial at Victoria Barracks this morning.
The insubordination clause was inserted owing to an alleged statement at a preliminary hearing of the case against him that he refused to soldier any more.
Lieut M. J. Richards on his behalf contended that it had not been proved that the prisoner was not on duty at any period during the days in question and as regarded the alleged insubordination as the statement attributed to the prisoner had been made during the hearing of the case he held that it was not evidence.

label: text
text: In explaining the resolutions prior to that after Mr. R. M. Dyer, Chief Manager, had read them, the Chairman had said:

label: text
text: Gentlemen,—The object of this meeting is to confirm as special resolutions the resolutions which were passed as extraordinary resolutions at the meeting of the Company held on May 18 last. As I then explained, the purpose of the resolutions is to raise further capital for the objects specified in the Chairman's speech at the annual general meeting held on March 30 last and in order to give effect to this it is necessary to alter Article 17 which at present limits the extent of a member's holding of shares. Sixty thousand of the new shares will be offered at once to the present shareholders at a premium of $10 per share in the manner indicated in the resolutions and the remaining—unissued shares will be subsequently dealt with as the Directors think fit.

label: text
text: I do not think there is anything further with which I need deal but if any shareholder would like to ask questions or seek any explanation, I shall be pleased to endeavour to answer such questions and give such explanation to the best of my ability.

label: text
text: It no questions are asked or explanation sought, I shall assume that you approve of the alterations in the Articles of Association as presented, and will thereupon propose the resolutions regarding the same which are set out in the notice convening this meeting.
